Subject: Lumenica Health — recap and quick ask on PII storage and TTL

Joshua / Meera,

Great to meet with the team this morning — thanks for the deep questions. Per our call, I wanted to capture the short list of follow-ups and ask for a single confirmation we can share with your security/compliance team.

Recap (quick):
- Scope: Lumenica will call Redwood’s hosted API for feature-flagged summarization and claim-extraction in patient intake flows.
- Expected volume: 5–10k requests/day in pilot, ramp to ~80k/day if pilot is green.
- Primary concerns you called out: persisted prompt contents, generated output storage, audit logs, retention TTLs, geographic residency, and encryption/access controls.

Can you confirm whether the answers below would be sufficient for your risk team? If not, flag the specific doc or evidence you need and we’ll get it to you.

What we propose to confirm:
- What Redwood stores by default for hosted customers (prompts, outputs, telemetry).
- TTL options we can offer (including immediate-nil retention for regulated pilots).
- Location options (default region vs. customer-pinned region).
- Access controls / encryption and who can see logs.

Attached is a one-page map (redwood-pii-map.pdf) that maps request/response fields to storage tiers — it’s intentionally high level for now.

Next steps: if that looks good I’ll pull together a short technical note (1 page) from our runtime/infra team spelling the exact storage locations and TTL knobs.

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the recap and the diagram. A few clarifying questions from our security team so we can determine risk and map to our procurement controls: 

1) Full prompt retention: Do you ever persist the full raw prompt text (unredacted) for hosted customers? If so, where and for how long?
2) Model outputs: Are generated outputs (model responses) stored? Are they part of the same retention policy as prompts?
3) Session/trace logs: What telemetry do you retain (request IDs, timestamps, user identifiers, IPs)? How long are traces held and what granularity is searchable?
4) Residency: Is data stored only in US regions by default? Can we require EU-only or a specific AWS region for a pilot?
5) TTL controls: Do you offer per-customer configurable TTLs and can TTL be set to 0 (zero retention) for prompts and outputs?
6) Encryption and access: Is data encrypted at rest with a customer-managed KMS option? Who at Redwood can access raw logs (SRE, Product, Eng)? Is access logged and audited?
7) Evidence: We’ll need either a short technical note + architecture diagram or a SOC2/third-party attestation pointing to these processes to move forward.

If you can answer the bullets above (even at a high level) that will help us determine whether to proceed with a short pilot.

—Joshua

Aditya / Monica —

Below is a concise, technical note we can send back to Joshua. I kept it factual and actionable; we should attach the short architecture sketch from infra and the deployment params file (deployment-ops-params.json).

Redwood technical note — prompt & output handling (hosted offering)

1) Raw prompt text
- Default: For hosted customers, full request payloads (raw prompt text) are stored in encrypted object storage for up to 30 days by default to support debugging, billing reconciliation, and quality monitoring.
- Opt-outs: For pilots with regulatory constraints we offer a zero-retention option (TTL=0) that prevents persisted prompt storage by routing requests to an ephemeral execution path; available as a configuration during pilot onboarding.

2) Model outputs (responses)
- Default: Generated outputs are stored alongside request metadata for 90 days by default to support tracing and evals.
- Customization: Retention for outputs can be reduced to 0, 7, 30, or 90 days per customer for hosted accounts; for strict customers we recommend the zero-retention pilot configuration.

3) Session & telemetry logs
- We capture request IDs, timestamps, model variant, token counts, and non-sensitive routing metadata by default. IP addresses and raw user identifiers are redacted unless the customer opts into expanded logging.
- Traces are retained for 90 days by default; sampling can be applied for high-volume customers and full traces can be disabled for compliance pilots.

4) Data residency
- Default storage region: us-east-1 (AWS) for hosted accounts.
- Region pinning: For pilot or enterprise customers we can pin storage and retained artifacts to a specific AWS region (e.g., eu-west-1) via account-level configuration.

5) Encryption and access controls
- Encryption: All persisted artifacts are encrypted at rest using AWS KMS. Customer-managed keys (CMKs) are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted customers we offer an option to enable a dedicated KMS key scoped to the tenant where operationally feasible.
- Access: Access to raw persisted logs is limited to a small, audited SRE/Infra group and is granted via time-limited tickets tied to an approval workflow. All access is logged and reviewed quarterly.

6) Evidence and attestation
- We can provide a short one-page architecture note + an export of relevant SOC2 control sections (where applicable). If you need formal attestation, we can arrange the specific artifact via our security team.

Action items for reply to Lumenica:
- Confirm they want a zero-retention pilot or one of the preset TTLs (0 / 7 / 30 / 90 days) for prompts and outputs.
- Ask which region they require for pinned storage (if any).
- Offer to provide the SOC2 excerpt and our short infra diagram as follow-up attachments.

I’ve attached deployment-ops-params.json with the explicit knobs we’ll hand to onboarding if they pick pilot configuration (includes TTL fields, region, and KMS selection).

If that looks good I recommend Aditya reply with a short paragraph and the two attachments.
